original_question: Let I = [0,1] be the unit interval with Lebesgue measure and the family of central symmetries s_c(x) = 2c - x. Calculate the maximal symmetry numbers ms_r(I), at least in the first nontrivial case r = 2.
target_in_paper: Section 6, Problem 6.4: "Calculate the values ms_r(I) (at least for r = 2)."
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the right object I = [0,1], the Lebesgue-measure setting, the relevant central symmetries s_c(x) = 2c - x, the quantity ms_r(I), and the paper’s emphasis on the first nontrivial case r = 2. This is very close to the paper’s official open problem in Section 6.
missing_details: The paper treats I = [0,1] as a measurable subset of the ambient symmetry measure space (R, lambda, S), where lambda is Lebesgue measure on R and S = {s_c : c in R}; it is not a standalone symmetry space preserved by every s_c.
The exact meaning of ms_r(I) should be stated: it is the maximal guaranteed measure of a monochromatic measurable S-symmetric subset that appears in every measurable r-coloring of I.
The quantifier on r should be explicit: r ranges over positive integers, with the paper specifically asking for all r and, at minimum, r = 2.
The colorings are required to be measurable r-colorings chi : I -> r.
A subset A must be measurable and satisfy A = s_c(A) for some c in R; equivalently, A is centrally symmetric about some center c.
Because the relevant symmetries are involutions, one can equivalently write ms(A) = sup over c in R of lambda(A ∩ s_c(A)); this is part of the nearby formalism defining ms_r.

The paper explicitly records the equivalent asymptotic discrete formulation ms_r(I) = lim_{n->infinity} ms_r(n)/n, where ms_r(n) is defined for the finite ordinal n = {0,1,...,n-1} with discrete central symmetries x -> c - x.
refined_question: For each integer r >= 1, determine the exact value of ms_r(I), where I = [0,1] is viewed as a measurable subset of the symmetry measure space (R, lambda, S) with lambda the Lebesgue measure and S = {s_c : c in R}, s_c(x) = 2c - x; equivalently, determine the largest epsilon such that every measurable r-coloring I = C_1 union ... union C_r contains a measurable monochromatic subset A subseteq C_i with lambda(A) >= epsilon and A = s_c(A) for some c in R. In particular, determine ms_2(I).
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, by Theorem 6.2(1), for each integer r >= 1 determine the asymptotic constant ms_r(I) = lim_{n->infinity} ms_r(n)/n = inf_{n in N} ms_r(n)/n, where ms_r(n) is the largest integer k such that every r-coloring of n = {0,1,...,n-1} contains a monochromatic subset A of cardinality at least k with A = c - A for some integer c.
justification: The draft is targeting Section 6, not the introduction: the official nearest formulation is exactly Problem 6.4. The surrounding text in Section 6 defines the ambient interval problem, explains that ms_r(I) is the supremal guaranteed measure of a monochromatic symmetric subset in every measurable r-coloring, and records the asymptotic equivalence with the discrete quantities ms_r(n). Theorem 6.1 and Theorem 6.2 give the paper’s current bounds and structure theory; in particular, Theorem 6.2(7) isolates the first nontrivial case with 0.15935 <= ms_2(I) < 5/24. The main incompleteness of the draft is that it does not explicitly define ms_r(I) in the paper’s formal Section 3 sense and does not make clear that I is a measurable subset of (R, lambda, S), which matters because most maps s_c do not preserve I as a set.
